mainTopic: Where the arm and head תפילין are placed, and whether the four ציציות are one מצוה or four
overview: The amud opens by finishing a question about a בכור born with two heads: since the תורה counts פדיון הבכור 'per skull,' this case is an exception. The גמרא then asks how we know the arm תפילין go on the upper arm. It gives three sources: a comparison to the head תפילין, 'a sign for you' (רבי אליעזר), and 'opposite the heart' (רבי יצחק). אמימר explains that 'a sign for you' only fixes the place, so visible תפילין are fine. Next, a ברייתא learns that the head תפילין go on the upper, hairy part of the head, from the איסור of a bald spot for the dead. רבי יהודה reaches the same result through the laws of צרעת. The גמרא then turns to the משנה on ציצית: are the four ציציות one מצוה or four? It offers three practical differences and rules that cutting, tying or sewing a corner does not remove the obligation. The final הלכה is not like רבי ישמעאל, as the story of מר בר רב אשי's torn ציצית shows. That story raises a challenge from כבוד הבריות, and רב בר שבא's answer begins here and continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The word 'yet' limits which firstborns are redeemed
steps.stepSummary: The tail end of a challenge: the word אך in the פסוק about redeeming a בכור comes to exclude some firstborns.
steps.simpleTranslation: The word 'yet' (אך) separates out a case: not every firstborn is redeemed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a challenge from the previous section about a baby born with two heads. The challenge uses the word אך to argue that such a baby should not need פדיון at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says 'אך פדה תפדה את בכור האדם,' and the word אך is read as a limiting word. It excludes a firstborn who is like a טריפה, one who will not survive. A two-headed baby seems to fit that category, so the challenge asks why he would need to be redeemed.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Yet / only.' A word that limits or excludes
It made a distinction; it separated out a case
Redeeming a firstborn son by giving the כהן five silver coins

phrases.english: "Yet" makes a distinction,
phrases.notes: This is the word אך in במדבר 18:15, 'yet you shall surely redeem the firstborn of man.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a challenge begun before this section, about the two-headed firstborn.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that a two-headed firstborn needs redemption (with ten סלעים)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: אך excludes a firstborn who cannot survive, and a two-headed baby is like that, so he should need no פדיון at all.

steps.title: Redemption depends on the skull
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the תורה ties פדיון הבכור to the skull (גלגלת), so a firstborn with two skulls is treated differently.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here it is different, because the Merciful One made it depend on the skull.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. This case is special because the תורה measures redemption 'per skull.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says 'five shekels per skull' (חמשת חמשת שקלים לגלגלת). That wording shows the תורה counts skulls, so a baby with two skulls is not simply excluded the way a טריפה would be. The general rule of אך still stands; this case is an exception because of the skull-based wording.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Here it is different.' The case at hand is an exception
Skull; head
The Merciful One (the תורה) made it depend on

steps.whatToRemember: פדיון הבכור is counted 'per skull,' so the two-headed case is a special exception to the rule of אך.

phrases.english: Here it is different,
since the Merciful One made it depend on the skull.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from אך.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the case based on the wording of the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A two-headed firstborn is like one who cannot survive, so he is excluded from redemption.
steps.terutzMaskana: Because the תורה counts by skull, the two-headed case is an exception and redemption applies.

steps.title: How do we know 'your arm' means the upper arm?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the ברייתא about תפילין and asks for the source that יד means the קיבורת (upper arm).
steps.simpleTranslation: The master said: 'Your arm' means the upper arm. From where do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to a line in the ברייתא about תפילין. It asks for the source that 'your יד' means the upper arm and not the hand.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word יד can mean either the hand or the arm. The ברייתא said it means the קיבורת, the bulge of the upper arm. The גמרא now wants to know what proves this.

keyTerms.meaning: The bicep, the thick muscle of the upper arm
'From where do we know this?' A request for a source
The תפילין worn on the arm

phrases.english: The master said: "Your arm" is the bicep.
From where do we know this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the two-headed firstborn discussion and returns to the main ברייתא about תפילין.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source that יד in the תפילין פסוק means the upper arm.

steps.title: Learning the arm from the head
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא compares the arm תפילין to the head תפילין: just as the head ones go on the high part of the head, the arm ones go on the high part of the arm.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages taught: 'On your arm' means the high part of the arm. Do you say that, or does it mean literally on the hand? The תורה said to put תפילין on the arm and on the head. Just as on the head it is the high part, here too it is the high part of the arm.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a ברייתא. It learns where the arm תפילין go by comparing them to the head תפילין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא first raises the other option, that יד means the actual hand. It rejects this with a comparison: the two kinds of תפילין are commanded together, so they follow the same pattern. Since the head תפילין go on the high part of the head, the arm תפילין go on the high part of the arm.

keyTerms.meaning: The raised or high part of the arm (the bicep)
Literally; actually
'Just as there, so too here.' A comparison between two cases

phrases.aramaic: דְּתָנוּ רַבָּנַן: ״עַל יָדְךָ״ – זוֹ גּוֹבַהּ שֶׁבַּיָּד.
phrases.english: As the Sages taught: "On your arm" is the high part of the arm.
Do you say it is the high part of the arm,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא עַל יָדְךָ מַמָּשׁ?
phrases.english: or is it only literally on your hand?
The Torah said: Put תפילין on the arm
and put תפילין on the head.
Just as there it is on the high part of the head,
so too here it is on the high part of the arm.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the מנלן question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A comparison to the head תפילין: both go on the high part of the body part they are placed on.

steps.title: A sign for you, not for others
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר says the comparison is not needed: 'a sign for you' means the תפילין go in a place seen by you and not by others, which is the upper arm.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר says: That is not needed, because the פסוק says 'It shall be a sign for you.' A sign for you, and not a sign for others.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר offers a different source for the same rule. He learns it from the words 'a sign for you.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: He reads 'for you' as excluding 'for others.' The arm תפילין must go in a spot that is normally covered, which is the upper arm, while the hand is normally visible. He reaches the same result as the ברייתא but from a different פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It is not needed.' This proof is unnecessary because there is a better one
'A sign for you'
'And not a sign for others'

phrases.english: רבי אליעזר says: It is not needed,
for it says: "And it shall be a sign for you"
a sign for you, and not a sign for others.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different derivation in place of the comparison to the head.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The arm תפילין go in a place that is a sign for the wearer and not for others, which is the upper arm.

steps.title: Placed opposite the heart
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק learns the location from 'place these words on your heart... and bind them': the תפילין must sit opposite the heart.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק says: That is not needed, because it says 'You shall place these words on your heart... and bind them.' The placing should be opposite the heart.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יצחק gives a third source for the same rule. He links the binding of תפילין to the heart.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק puts 'on your heart' and 'bind them' next to each other. רבי יצחק reads this as saying the arm תפילין must be placed facing the heart. The upper arm rests against the side near the heart, so that is the spot.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Placing.' Here it means putting on the תפילין
Opposite or facing the heart
'And you shall bind them'

phrases.english: רבי יצחק says: It is not needed,

phrases.aramaic: הֲרֵי הוּא אוֹמֵר: ״וְשַׂמְתֶּם אֶת דְּבָרַי אֵלֶּה
phrases.english: for it says: "You shall place these words of Mine
on your heart... and you shall bind them"
phrases.notes: דברים 11:18. The dots skip a few words of the פסוק.

phrases.english: meaning the placing should be opposite the heart.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third derivation for the same location.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The arm תפילין must be placed opposite the heart, which means on the upper arm.
steps.whatToRemember: Three sources lead to one result, the upper arm: comparison to the head, 'a sign for you,' and 'opposite the heart.'

steps.title: Aiming the תפילין toward the heart
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא and רב אחא בריה דרב אויא would carefully place the arm תפילין facing the heart.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא and רב אחא son of רב אויא would aim and place it facing the heart.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reports how some אמוראים actually put on their תפילין, following רבי יצחק's idea of 'opposite the heart.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: Their practice shows that 'opposite the heart' was carried out in real life. They did more than put the תפילין on the upper arm; they angled them so they faced the heart.

keyTerms.meaning: He aims or lines it up carefully
Facing his heart

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי חִיָּיא וְרַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אַוְיָא
phrases.english: רבי חייא and רב אחא son of רב אויא
would aim it and place it facing his heart.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows רבי יצחק's derivation carried out in practice.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In practice the arm תפילין are aimed toward the heart.

steps.title: רב אשי sees אמימר's תפילין showing
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי noticed that אמימר's תפילין were visible through a tear in his sleeve and asked: don't you hold 'a sign for you and not for others'?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי was sitting before אמימר. There was a tear in his sleeve, and the תפילין could be seen. He said to him: Doesn't the master hold 'a sign for you, and not a sign for others'?
steps.whatsHappening: A story raises a challenge. רב אשי sees אמימר's תפילין showing and asks whether this goes against רבי אליעזר's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אשי reads 'not a sign for others' as a rule that the תפילין must stay hidden. If so, תפילין visible through a tear would be a problem.

keyTerms.meaning: A tear or slit, here in the sleeve
They were visible
'Doesn't the master hold this view?' A challenge to a sage's conduct

phrases.aramaic: רַב אָשֵׁי הֲוָה יָתֵיב קַמֵּיהּ דְּאַמֵּימָר,
phrases.english: רב אשי was sitting before אמימר.
There was a tear on his arm,
phrases.notes: The tear was in the sleeve covering אמימר's arm.

phrases.english: and the תפילין could be seen.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: לָא סָבַר לַהּ מָר
phrases.english: He said to him: Doesn't the master hold
"a sign for you," and not a sign for others?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses רבי אליעזר's derivation to question אמימר's behavior.
steps.kashyaTarget: אמימר wearing תפילין that others could see
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If תפילין must be 'not a sign for others,' they must be kept hidden, and visible תפילין break that rule.

steps.title: It tells us the place, not that they must be hidden
steps.stepSummary: אמימר answers that 'a sign for you' defines the location (a spot normally covered), not a requirement that the תפילין stay hidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: It was said about the place that is 'a sign for you.'
steps.whatsHappening: אמימר answers רב אשי. The rule 'a sign for you' only tells us where to put the תפילין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase picks out a spot on the body that is normally covered, the upper arm. Once the תפילין are in that spot, it does not matter if someone happens to see them.

keyTerms.meaning: In the place of; regarding the location

steps.whatToRemember: 'לך לאות ולא לאחרים לאות' sets the location of the arm תפילין (the upper arm). It does not require that they be kept out of sight.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't read 'not a sign for others' as 'תפילין must always be hidden.' אמימר says it only defines the place on the arm.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains why תפילין that are visible on the upper arm are not a problem. The rule is about where you put them, not about hiding them.

phrases.english: He said to him: It was said regarding the place that is "a sign for you."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב אשי's challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the scope of the rule
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Not a sign for others' means the תפילין must stay hidden.
steps.terutzMaskana: It only fixes the location, the normally covered upper arm. Being seen there is fine.

steps.title: What is the source for the upper part of the head?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how we know the head תפילין go on the upper part of the head.
steps.simpleTranslation: The upper part of the head: where do we learn this from?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to the head תפילין and asks for the source of their location. This question sets up the ברייתא that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier steps dealt with where the arm תפילין go. Now the גמרא needs a source for the head. The פסוק says 'between your eyes', so it is not obvious that it means higher up on the head.

keyTerms.meaning: The upper part of the head, where the hair grows
From where do we know this?

phrases.english: The upper part of the head: from where do we derive it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After finishing the arm תפילין, the גמרא opens the parallel question for the head.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source that the head תפילין go on the upper part of the head and not literally between the eyes.

steps.title: Learning it from the איסור of a bald spot for the dead
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא compares 'between your eyes' by תפילין to 'between your eyes' in the איסור of making a bald spot for the dead. That bald spot is on the upper head, so the תפילין go there too.
steps.simpleTranslation: As the רבנן taught: 'Between your eyes' means the upper part of the head. You say it is the upper part of the head, but maybe it means literally between your eyes? It says here 'between your eyes', and it says there 'Do not make a bald spot between your eyes for the dead.' Just as there it means the upper head, where one can make a bald spot, so too here it means the upper head, where one can make a bald spot.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a ברייתא that uses the same words, 'between your eyes', in two places. Since the bald-spot פסוק clearly means the hairy upper head, the תפילין פסוק means the same.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא first raises the obvious option that 'between your eyes' is meant literally. It then rules that out with a word comparison. You can only make a bald spot where hair grows, so 'between your eyes' must mean the upper head.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Between your eyes', the Torah's phrase for where the head תפילין go
Literally, exactly
A bald spot made by pulling out hair in mourning, which the Torah forbids
'It says here... and it says there': a comparison of the same word in two פסוקים

steps.confusionAlert: Do not take 'between your eyes' literally. The הלכה is that the head תפילין go above the forehead, where the hair starts, not on the bridge of the nose.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the practical הלכה of where the head תפילין are worn.

phrases.english: As the Sages taught:
'Between your eyes': this is the upper part of the head.
Do you say this is the upper part of the head,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא בֵּין עֵינֶיךָ מַמָּשׁ?
phrases.english: or is it only literally between your eyes?
It is stated here 'between your eyes',
and it is stated there:
'Do not make a bald spot between your eyes for the dead.'
Just as there it is on the upper part of the head,
a place where one can make a bald spot,
so too here it is on the upper part of the head,
a place where one can make a bald spot.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 10 with a ברייתא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A word comparison of 'between your eyes' to the bald-spot איסור teaches that the head תפילין go on the upper, hair-growing part of the head.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: compare head to arm, a place for only one kind of צרעת
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה says the bald-spot comparison is not needed. The arm תפילין go on a spot that can only become טמא with one kind of נגע, so the head תפילין must go on such a spot too.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: It is not needed. The Torah said to put תפילין on the arm and to put תפילין on the head. Just as there it is a place that can become טמא with only one kind of נגע, so too here it is a place that can become טמא with only one kind of נגע.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה gives a different source for the head location. He compares the head תפילין to the arm תפילין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The arm is plain skin, so it can only get the skin type of צרעת. The hairy part of the head can only get the head type of צרעת. So the head תפילין belong on a spot that, like the arm, has just one type of נגע.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not needed: the earlier proof is unnecessary
To become טמא (ritually impure)
A mark of צרעת that can make a person טמא

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says: It is not necessary;
the Torah said: 'Put תפילין on the arm',
phrases.notes: This isn't an exact פסוק. רבי יהודה is just summing up the Torah's two commands, arm and head.

phrases.english: 'Put תפילין on the head';
just as there it is in a place that is fit
to become impure with one kind of mark,
phrases.notes: The arm can only get the skin kind of צרעת.

phrases.english: so too here it is in a place that is fit
to become impure with one kind of mark.
phrases.notes: The hairy part of the head can only get the head kind of צרעת.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different derivation in place of the ברייתא's bald-spot comparison.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The head תפילין, like the arm תפילין, go on a spot that can become טמא with only one type of נגע.

steps.title: Why the actual space between the eyes is ruled out
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה's rule excludes the literal spot between the eyes. That spot has both skin and eyebrow hair, so it can get two kinds of צרעת: white hair and yellow hair.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is to exclude the actual space between your eyes, where there is both flesh and hair. There, a white hair can make it טמא, and a yellow hair can also make it טמא.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה continues and spells out what his rule takes out: the real spot between the eyes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Between the eyes there is skin and eyebrow hair. White hair is a sign of skin צרעת, and yellow hair is a sign of head צרעת. Two kinds of נגע can happen there, so it fails רבי יהודה's 'one kind' test.

keyTerms.meaning: To exclude, to rule out
White hair, a sign of skin צרעת
Yellow hair, a sign of head or beard צרעת

steps.whatToRemember: Both the ברייתא and רבי יהודה agree that the head תפילין go on the upper, hairy part of the head. They only argue about the source.

phrases.english: This excludes the literal 'between your eyes',
where there is flesh and hair,
phrases.notes: The hair here is the eyebrows.

phrases.english: so there can be white hair,
and there can also be yellow hair.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains what רבי יהודה's comparison comes to exclude.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The literal space between the eyes is excluded because it can get two types of נגע.

steps.title: The משנה: the four ציציות hold each other back
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה: missing any one of the four ציציות stops the מצוה, because all four are one מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The four ציציות hold each other back, because all four of them are one מצוה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new topic and quotes the משנה's line about ציצית. This quote sets up the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא holds that the four ציציות are one combined מצוה, so without all four you have not done the מצוה at all. The משנה also brings רבי ישמעאל, who holds they are four separate מצוות.

keyTerms.meaning: The fringes on the four corners of a garment
Hold each other back: missing one makes the others not count
One single מצוה

phrases.aramaic: אַרְבַּע צִיצִיּוֹת מְעַכְּבוֹת זוֹ אֶת זוֹ,
phrases.english: The four ציציות hold each other back,
as the four of them are one מצוה.
phrases.notes: The משנה goes on with רבי ישמעאל's view that they are four separate מצוות. The גמרא assumes you know it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַרְבַּע צִיצִיּוֹת מְעַכְּבוֹת זוֹ אֶת זוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, moving from תפילין to ציצית.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: All four ציציות are one מצוה, so each one is needed for the others to count.

steps.title: What is the practical difference between the views?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what practical difference there is between the תנא קמא and רבי ישמעאל.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the difference between them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for a case where the two views would lead to different results. This sets up רב יוסף's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Either way, a person wearing fewer than four ציציות lacks something. The גמרא wants a concrete case where 'one מצוה' versus 'four מצוות' actually changes the הלכה.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the practical difference between them?

phrases.english: What is the difference between them?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the מחלוקת in the משנה just quoted.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A practical case where the תנא קמא and רבי ישמעאל would rule differently.

steps.title: רב יוסף: a linen sheet with ציצית
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף says the difference is a linen sheet with wool ציציות. With fewer than four, the תנא קמא forbids wearing it because of כלאים, while רבי ישמעאל permits it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: A linen sheet with ציצית is the difference between them.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף names the case where the two views differ: a linen garment with wool ציציות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Wool on linen is כלאים, which is allowed only when the ציצית מצוה is being done. If fewer than four ציציות are on the sheet, the תנא קמא says no מצוה is being done at all, so wearing it is forbidden. רבי ישמעאל says each fringe is its own מצוה, so the כלאים is still allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: A linen sheet or garment
The איסור of wearing wool and linen together

steps.whatToRemember: The 'one מצוה versus four מצוות' debate matters for כלאים: only a real ציצית מצוה permits wool fringes on linen.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
A linen sheet with ציצית is the difference between them.
phrases.notes: Picture linen with wool ציציות and fewer than four on it. The question is whether wearing it is still allowed despite כלאים.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: סָדִין בְּצִיצִית אִיכָּא בֵּינַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 15.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The difference is a linen sheet with wool ציציות but fewer than four: forbidden according to the תנא קמא and permitted according to רבי ישמעאל.

steps.title: A second answer: a five-cornered garment
steps.stepSummary: רבא בר אהינא says the practical difference between the תנא קמא and רבי ישמעאל is a טלית with five corners.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא בר אהינא said: The difference between them is a cloak with five corners.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second answer to the question of step 15. רבא בר אהינא says the two opinions disagree about a garment that has five corners.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Such a garment needs ציצית, but the question is whether the fifth corner also needs them. If each ציצית is its own מצוה (רבי ישמעאל), every corner, including the fifth, needs one. If all four together make one מצוה (תנא קמא), the obligation covers only four corners.

keyTerms.meaning: There is a difference between them; the practical case where two opinions lead to different results
A cloak with five corners

phrases.english: Rava bar Ahina said:
a cloak with five corners
is the difference between them.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא בַּר אֲהִינָא אָמַר: טַלִּית בַּעֲלַת חָמֵשׁ אִיכָּא בֵּינַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different answer than רב יוסף's (step 16) to the same question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The difference is whether a fifth corner needs ציצית: according to רבי ישמעאל it does, and according to the תנא קמא only four corners are covered.

steps.title: A third answer: carrying on שבת in a garment missing ציציות
steps.stepSummary: רבינא says the difference is רב הונא's ruling that someone who goes out on שבת wearing a garment without all its proper ציציות must bring a חטאת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: The difference between them is the ruling of רב הונא. רב הונא said: Someone who goes out on שבת in a cloak that does not have its proper ציציות must bring a sin offering.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a third answer to the question of step 15. רבינא says the two opinions disagree about רב הונא's ruling on carrying on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a garment lacks some ציציות, the ones that are there do not fulfill any מצוה according to the תנא קמא. They are just a load being carried into the public domain, so the person must bring a חטאת. According to רבי ישמעאל each ציצית is its own מצוה, so the strings are part of the garment and he is not liable.

keyTerms.meaning: Having its ציציות properly, as the law requires
Must bring a sin offering, the קרבן brought for breaking שבת by mistake
One who goes out into the public domain

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the question of 'one מצוה or four' affects more than ציצית itself. It can decide whether a person broke שבת.

phrases.english: Ravina said:
The ruling of Rav Huna is the difference between them,
as Rav Huna said:
One who goes out in a cloak
that does not have its ציציות properly
on שבת –
is liable to bring a sin offering.
phrases.notes: This is because the strings that are there don't count as a מצוה, so they're just something being carried outside.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבִינָא אָמַר: דְּרַב הוּנָא אִיכָּא בֵּינַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third answer to the same question, after רב יוסף and רבא בר אהינא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב הונא's ruling follows the תנא קמא. According to רבי ישמעאל, the existing ציציות are a מצוה and not a load, so there is no חטאת.

steps.title: Cutting off a corner does not remove the ציצית obligation
steps.stepSummary: רב שישא בריה דרב אידי rules that someone who cuts a corner off his garment has accomplished nothing, because he has just made it a five-cornered garment.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שישא son of רב אידי said: Someone who cuts a corner off his garment has done nothing, because he has made it a cloak with five corners.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ruling. Trying to get out of ציצית by cutting off a corner of the garment does not work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Cutting off a corner does not remove it. It turns one corner into two, so the garment now has five corners. A five-cornered garment (the case from step 17) still needs ציצית, so nothing was gained.

keyTerms.meaning: Who cut off (a corner of it)
A garment or cloak
He has done nothing at all; it has no effect

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב שִׁישָׁא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִידִי:
phrases.english: Rav Sheisha son of Rav Idi said:
One who cuts off a corner of his garment –
has not done anything at all,
he has made it a cloak with five corners.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב שִׁישָׁא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִידִי: הַאי מַאן דְּבַצְּרֵיהּ לִגְלִימֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Picks up the five-cornered garment from step 17 and applies it to a practical case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Cutting off a corner leaves the garment with five corners, and it still needs ציצית.

steps.title: Tying up a corner does not remove the ציצית obligation
steps.stepSummary: רב משרשיא rules that someone who ties up a corner of his garment has accomplished nothing, because a tied corner counts as if it were untied.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב משרשיא said: Someone who ties up his garment has done nothing. What is the reason? It is as if it were untied.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a similar ruling. Trying to get out of ציצית by tying or knotting a corner of the garment does not work either.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A knot can be opened at any time, so the הלכה treats the tied corner as still being a normal corner. The garment keeps its four corners and still needs ציצית.

keyTerms.meaning: Who tied it up
What is the reason?
It is treated as if it were untied

phrases.english: Rav Mesharshiya said:
One who ties up his garment –
has not done anything at all.
What is the reason?
Because it is considered as though it is untied.
phrases.notes: A knot can always be undone, so the corner still counts as a corner.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב מְשַׁרְשְׁיָא: הַאי מַאן דְּצַיְּירֵיהּ לִגְלִימֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel ruling to step 19, this time about tying a corner instead of cutting it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A tied corner is treated as untied, so the garment still needs ציצית.

steps.title: Support from a משנה about tied leather jugs
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא backs up רב משרשיא with a משנה: tied leather jugs are not considered real vessels, because a knot is expected to be opened. The exception is Arab jugs, which are tied permanently.
steps.simpleTranslation: And we also learned in a משנה: All tied leather jugs are טהור, except for those of the Arabs.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a משנה to support רב משרשיא's idea that a knot is treated as if it were untied.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A leather jug whose bottom is only tied shut is not a real vessel, because the knot will be opened. That is why it cannot become טמא. Arabs tied theirs permanently, so those jugs count as vessels. The same logic shows that a normal knot in a garment does not change the garment.

keyTerms.meaning: Leather jugs that are tied shut instead of sewn
Pure; here, unable to become טמא because they are not real vessels
Arabs, who tied their jugs with a permanent knot

steps.whatToRemember: Cutting off or tying up a corner does not get a garment out of ציצית. A cut makes five corners, and a knot counts as if it were untied, just as tied leather jugs are not real vessels.

phrases.english: And we also learned in a משנה:
All tied leather jugs are pure,
phrases.notes: These jugs aren't considered real vessels, because their knots are expected to be opened.

phrases.english: except for those of the Arabs.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּתְנַן נָמֵי: כׇּל חֲמָתוֹת הַצְּרוּרוֹת טְהוֹרוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the reasoning of step 20 with a משנה.
steps.raayaObject: רב משרשיא's principle that a tied item counts as if it were untied.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה about tied leather jugs being טהור, except Arab jugs with permanent knots.

steps.title: Sewing up a corner does not remove the ציצית obligation
steps.stepSummary: רב דימי מנהרדעא rules that someone who folds and sews up part of his garment has done nothing. If he really did not want that part, he would cut it off and throw it away.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב דימי of נהרדעא said: Someone who sews up his garment has done nothing. If he really did not need that part, let him cut it off and throw it away.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the last ruling in a series about tricks that try to get a garment out of needing ציצית. רב דימי says sewing a corner closed does not work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב דימי's reason is different from the knot reasoning in Step 20. If he truly did not want that part of the garment, he would cut it off and throw it away. Since he keeps it, it still counts as part of the garment, and the original corners still need ציצית.

keyTerms.meaning: he sewed it
a cloak or garment
he has not done anything that counts
let him cut it and throw it away

steps.whatToRemember: Cutting off a corner (Step 19), tying it (Step 20), and sewing it (Step 22) all fail to free a garment from ציצית.

phrases.english: Rav Dimi of Neharde'a said:
One who sews up his garment
phrases.notes: He folded over part of a long garment and sewed it closed, hoping to get rid of a corner.

phrases.english: has not done anything,
if it is so that he does not need it,
let him cut it off and throw it away.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a third failed method (sewing) to cutting and tying.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sewing up part of a garment does not change its corners; it still needs ציצית on the original corners.

steps.title: שמואל rules like רבי ישמעאל that the four ציציות are four separate מצוות
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה again: רבי ישמעאל says the four ציציות are four separate מצוות. רב יהודה reports in the name of שמואל that the הלכה follows רבי ישמעאל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ישמעאל says: The four of them are four מצוות. רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: The הלכה is like רבי ישמעאל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה and quotes רבי ישמעאל's opinion. Then it brings שמואל's ruling that the הלכה follows him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי ישמעאל, each corner's ציצית is its own מצוה. If one is missing, you still get credit for the others. The תנא קמא holds that missing one ruins the whole מצוה. שמואל sides with רבי ישמעאל.

keyTerms.meaning: the four of them (the four corners' ציציות)
four separate מצוות; one missing does not cancel the others
the practical law follows this opinion

phrases.english: Rabbi Yishmael says:
The four of them are four מצוות.
Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
The halakha is like Rabbi Yishmael.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל אוֹמֵר: אַרְבַּעְתָּן אַרְבַּע מִצְוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the tricks for removing corners and goes back to the משנה's argument between the תנא קמא and רבי ישמעאל.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to שמואל, the הלכה follows רבי ישמעאל: each ציצית is a separate מצוה.

steps.title: The final הלכה is not like רבי ישמעאל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא states that, despite שמואל's ruling, the final הלכה does not follow רבי ישמעאל.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the הלכה is not like him.
steps.whatsHappening: Right after quoting שמואל, the גמרא gives its own final word: the הלכה is not like רבי ישמעאל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This overturns שמואל's ruling for practical purposes. The final הלכה follows the תנא קמא: all four ציציות work together, so if one is missing, the garment is not a proper ציצית garment. The story in the next step shows this in action.

keyTerms.meaning: there is not
the practical law
like him (רבי ישמעאל)

steps.confusionAlert: This line does not contradict itself. שמואל ruled like רבי ישמעאל, but the גמרא's own final ruling rejects שמואל's view.

phrases.english: But the halakha is not like him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sets aside שמואל's ruling from Step 23.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The final הלכה follows the תנא קמא: the four ציציות depend on one another.

steps.title: מר בר רב אשי would have taken off his garment when a ציצית tore
steps.stepSummary: While רבינא walked behind מר בר רב אשי on a festival שבת, a corner of מר בר רב אשי's ציצית tore, and רבינא stayed quiet. At the house, רבינא told him. מר בר רב אשי answered that had he known, he would have thrown off the garment right there.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא was walking behind מר בר רב אשי on the שבת of the festival. The corner holding his ציצית tore, and רבינא said nothing. When they reached his house, רבינא told him: It tore back there. מר בר רב אשי said: If you had told me, I would have thrown it off right there.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story that shows the final הלכה from Step 24 in practice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מר בר רב אשי treats a garment with one torn ציצית as no longer a proper ציצית garment. That is the תנא קמא's view, not רבי ישמעאל's. On שבת in the street, wearing such a garment would be a problem, so he would have taken it off at once.

keyTerms.meaning: the שבת of the festival, when the rabbi gave a public lecture
corner
it tore off
I would have thrown it off

steps.whyThisMatters: It sets up the challenge in the next step: is taking off your garment in public really allowed, given how embarrassing that is?

phrases.english: Ravina was walking
behind Mar bar Rav Ashi
on the Shabbat of the festival,
the corner holding his fringe tore,
and he did not say anything to him.
When he arrived at his house,
he said to him: It tore back there.
He said to him: If you had told me,
I would have thrown it off right there.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבִינָא הֲוָה קָא אָזֵיל אַבָּתְרֵיהּ דְּמָר בַּר רַב אָשֵׁי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows the ruling of Step 24 in a real-life case.
steps.raayaObject: The final הלכה is not like רבי ישמעאל; one torn ציצית ruins the garment.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The behavior of מר בר רב אשי, who would have removed the garment immediately.

steps.title: Challenge: doesn't כבוד הבריות override a prohibition of the תורה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how מר בר רב אשי could take off his garment in public. There is a known rule that human dignity is so important it pushes aside a prohibition of the תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't the Master say: Great is human dignity, because it pushes aside a prohibition in the תורה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges מר בר רב אשי's statement from the story. Undressing in the street is embarrassing, and dignity should override the prohibition.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Taking off a garment in public is a loss of dignity. Since כבוד הבריות can push aside a לא תעשה, he should have been allowed to keep wearing it until he got home. The next step begins the גמרא's answer.

keyTerms.meaning: human dignity; not embarrassing people
pushes aside, overrides
a negative commandment, a prohibition

phrases.english: But didn't the Master say:
Great is human dignity,
as it overrides a prohibition in the Torah?
phrases.notes: Here the prohibition would be carrying in the street on שבת by wearing a garment that no longer counts properly.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא אָמַר מָר: גָּדוֹל כְּבוֹד הַבְּרִיּוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks מר בר רב אשי's statement that he would have thrown off the garment.
steps.kashyaTarget: מר בר רב אשי's statement that he would have removed his garment in public.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Removing a garment in public hurts one's dignity, and כבוד הבריות overrides a prohibition of the תורה, so he should not have had to remove it.

steps.title: רב בר שבא begins explaining the human-dignity rule
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא starts its answer to the question about כבוד הבריות. רב בר שבא explained that rule in front of רב כהנא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב בר שבא explained it in front of רב כהנא:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its answer to the last question. It tells us that רב בר שבא explained the rule about human dignity while sitting before רב כהנא, and the explanation itself comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question was that כבוד הבריות should have stopped מר בר רב אשי from undressing in public. The word תרגמה shows that the answer will not throw out that rule. Instead, it will explain more narrowly which kind of prohibition human dignity pushes aside.

keyTerms.meaning: He explained it. Literally 'he translated it.' A sage reads an earlier statement in a more exact way to solve a problem.
In front of him, before him. Usually a student speaking in the presence of his teacher.
Human dignity. This is the rule being explained here.

steps.confusionAlert: This line is not the full answer. It only tells us who explained the rule. What the rule really means comes right after.

phrases.english: Rav bar Shabba explained it
phrases.notes: 'It' is the rule from the last question, that human dignity pushes aside a prohibition of the תורה.

phrases.english: before Rav Kahana:

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּרְגְּומַהּ רַב בַּר שְׁבָא קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב כָּהֲנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the answer to the question in step 26 by bringing in רב בר שבא's explanation of the כבוד הבריות rule.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the rule: the כבוד הבריות principle will be read so that it does not apply here.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought כבוד הבריות pushes aside every prohibition of the תורה, so מר בר רב אשי should have kept his garment on in public.
steps.terutzMaskana: The rule will be explained as having a limited reach. The details come in the next line.
